plain.li: First night here. I want to write down what I make of the place now, before I get used to it.
They gave me a bed and a bowl of bean stew. I've had worse first days.
[winter] Came in out of the snow with my boots soaked through. They put a hot bowl in my hands and didn't ask many questions.

warm.li: The people here look worn out, and they still made room for me at the table. I think I'll like it.

blunt.li: Day one. They need hands, I need a roof. Fair trade.

cheerful.li: First day here! I've learned most of their names already, and which one makes the bread.

gloomy.li: Another place to start over. I hope this one holds together longer than the last.

cold.li: The colony is understaffed and poorly defended. It will do for now.

plain.li: One of the others keeps a journal, so I'm trying it. I'm not sure what goes in one.
Starting a journal. If I die, at least someone will know what I thought of the rice.

warm.li: I want to remember these people. Writing them down seemed like the way to do it.

blunt.li: Started a journal. Don't expect much.

cheerful.li: Dear journal! I'm going to fill every page of you, starting with today's very good soup.

gloomy.li: A record, for whoever finds it. Hello, whoever you are.

cold.li: Keeping records improves decisions. Beginning now.

plain.li: They came through on "{WISH}". I hadn't expected them to bother.
I asked, and they did it. That goes in the journal, since it doesn't happen often.
[bitter] They finally did one thing I asked: {WISH}. It doesn't make up for the rest.

warm.li: They listened to me. I had to go and sit down for a while afterward.

blunt.li: Got what I wanted. About time.

cheerful.li: They said yes! I've been grinning at people all day like an idiot.

gloomy.li: Got a yes from the council. I keep waiting for the catch.

cold.li: Request fulfilled. The council is more reliable than I estimated.

plain.li: They promised, and they did it. I'm putting it here for the next time I doubt them.
They kept the promise about "{WISH}". It took a while, but they kept it.

warm.li: They kept their word. I went round after supper and thanked each of them.

blunt.li: They said they would. They did. Good.

cheerful.li: They kept their promise! I've told three people already.

gloomy.li: A promise kept. I'd almost stopped believing in those.

cold.li: Commitment honored. Trust adjusted upward.

plain.li: I asked and waited, and nothing came of it. I'll stop asking soon.
The days ran out and the council never got to it. So that's how it is.
[repeat] Asked a second time and got ignored a second time. I'm keeping count in here.

warm.li: I know they're busy. It still stings.

blunt.li: Ignored. I'll remember that the next time they want something from me.

cheerful.li: Oh well, no luck this time! I'll ask again after the harvest.

gloomy.li: I waited and no answer came. I wasn't really expecting one.

cold.li: Request lapsed. Lowering expectations accordingly.

plain.li: They looked me in the eye and promised. I'm putting the date down here so I don't forget it.
They promised, and the days ran out anyway. I waited up on the last night like a fool.

warm.li: I believed them because I wanted to. I don't know what to think now.

blunt.li: Liars, the lot of them.

cheerful.li: They broke their promise. Well, there's still stew tonight, and the weather's held.

gloomy.li: Of course they broke it. What else was ever going to happen?

cold.li: Promise broken. I won't take the council's word at face value again.

plain.li: They said no, to my face. Better than being strung along for weeks.
Refused. I'll get by without it.

warm.li: A clear no. I can respect that, even if I don't like it.

blunt.li: No, they said. Fine. Their loss.

cheerful.li: They said no! Oh well. I'll ask again after they've had a good dinner.

gloomy.li: They said no. It's still better than being ignored.

cold.li: Request declined. A clear answer, at least. I can plan around a clear answer.

plain.li: Finally, {DECREE}. I've been saying we needed it for weeks.
They declared {DECREE} today. There was grumbling at dinner, but not from me.

warm.li: A good decision today. I hope the others come round to it.

blunt.li: So it's {DECREE}. Finally. The complainers can complain.

cheerful.li: Good news today, it's {DECREE}! I whistled through every chore.

gloomy.li: For once the council did what I'd have done. It won't last.

cold.li: They chose {DECREE}. Correct.

plain.li: Now it's {DECREE}. They didn't ask what I thought.
The council declared {DECREE} today. Counting the days until it ends.

warm.li: I'll go along with it for the others' sake. I don't like it.

blunt.li: Whoever came up with {DECREE} can do my share.

cheerful.li: New decree, and I hate it! I'm still going to have a nice evening.

gloomy.li: Another rule. I'll get used to it, like I get used to everything here.

cold.li: They declared {DECREE} against my judgment. Noted for later.

plain.li: The council declared {DECREE} again and I couldn't take it. I don't remember all of what I did. I'm not as sorry as I should be.
We'd barely got through {DECREE} and they ordered it again. I'd had enough, and I let them all know it.
[night] Can't sleep. Keep thinking about the council, and {DECREE}, and the look on their faces when I snapped.

warm.li: I lost my temper over {DECREE}. Tomorrow I'll apologize to the ones I frightened.

blunt.li: They pushed {DECREE} on us one time too many. Now they know.

cheerful.li: So there is a limit to how much {DECREE} I can smile through. I found it today.

gloomy.li: Again it's {DECREE}, and it'll be {DECREE} next time too. I couldn't bear it anymore.

cold.li: The council repeated {DECREE} against all sense. My reaction was proportionate.

plain.li: I stopped waiting for the council and sorted it out myself. Took the afternoon.
Stopped complaining and did it myself. My back hurts, but it's done.
[night] Sorted out the thing that's been nagging at me. Maybe tonight I'll actually sleep.
[child] I did it all by myself, without asking a grown-up.

warm.li: Sorted it out myself today, then put a pot of tea on for whoever walked by.

blunt.li: Fixed it myself. Done.

cheerful.li: Took matters into my own hands today! It was a small matter, but it's sorted.

gloomy.li: I fixed one thing myself. There are a hundred more like it.

cold.li: I resolved it myself rather than wait on the council. Faster, and no favors owed.

plain.li: Married {OTHER_nameDef} today. I keep looking at my hands as if they should look different.
We said our vows outside, with the others watching. {OTHER_nameDef} said them louder than I did.
[night] Married. The word still sounds like it belongs to someone else.
{OTHER_nameDef} wore flowers in {OTHER_possessive} hair. I wore my only clean shirt.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I are married. Whatever comes next, it comes for both of us now.

blunt.li: Married {OTHER_nameDef}. Best decision I've made out here.

cheerful.li: Married to {OTHER_nameDef}! I've been smiling so long my face hurts.

gloomy.li: Married {OTHER_nameDef} today. I'm trying not to wait for it to go wrong.

cold.li: Formalized my partnership with {OTHER_nameDef}. A sensible arrangement. My hands shook during the vows, which I hadn't planned for.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} are married. I cried more than I expected to.
Watched {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} wed today. The colony felt like a village for an afternoon.
Ate too much at {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}'s wedding. My feet still ache from the dancing.

warm.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} married today. I hadn't seen {A_nameDef} smile like that before.

blunt.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} got married. Good for them. The food was decent.

cheerful.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} are married! I danced until my feet gave out.

gloomy.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} are married. I'm glad for them. I'm not sure I'll ever have that.

cold.li: Attended the union of {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}. Morale effects appear positive.

plain.li: {BABY_nameDef} is here. So small. I counted the fingers twice.
I'm a parent now. {BABY_nameDef} hasn't stopped crying, and I haven't stopped looking.
[night] {BABY_nameDef} is asleep at last. I'm too afraid to breathe in case it wakes them.
{BABY_nameDef} grabbed my finger today and wouldn't let go.

warm.li: Welcome, {BABY_nameDef}. We'll make this place worth growing up in.

blunt.li: {BABY_nameDef} was born today. Healthy. Loud. Mine.

cheerful.li: {BABY_nameDef} was born today! I keep telling people, even the ones who were there.

gloomy.li: {BABY_nameDef} was born into all this. I'll have to be better than the world is.

cold.li: {BABY_nameDef} arrived today, healthy and a good weight. I held {BABY_objective} longer than I needed to.

plain.li: Home after {DAYS} on the road. The colony looks smaller than I remembered, and better.
Back home. My own bed again after {DAYS}. I fell asleep with my boots on.
[winter] Home, out of the cold at last. {DAYS} of bad roads and worse weather, and I'd still go again.
Back after {DAYS}. I ate two bowls of stew standing up in the kitchen.

warm.li: Home after {DAYS}. They came out to the gate to meet us. I hadn't known I'd missed them this much.

blunt.li: Back after {DAYS}. Long trip. Good to be home.

cheerful.li: Home after {DAYS}, and I have so many stories! I started telling them before I'd put my pack down.

gloomy.li: Home after {DAYS}. Nothing burned down while we were gone. I'd half expected it to.

cold.li: Returned after {DAYS}. The expedition met most of its aims. I slept nine hours.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} broke today. I saw it coming and kept my mouth shut.
I'm worried about {OTHER_nameDef}. It's been building for weeks, and today it all came out.
Found {OTHER_nameDef} sitting out behind the storeroom tonight. I sat down too, and we didn't talk.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} had a terrible day. Tomorrow I'll sit with {OTHER_objective}, whether {OTHER_pronoun} wants company or not.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} cracked. Can't blame {OTHER_objective}, the way things are.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} had a really bad day. Tomorrow I'm baking {OTHER_objective} a berry pie.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} broke today. I wonder which of us is next.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} broke down today. The signs were there. I'll pay closer attention.

plain.li: {YEARS} year(s) here today. I've stopped thinking of anywhere else as home.
Anniversary today. A couple of the others remembered, which I didn't expect.

warm.li: Another year with these people. I'm lucky, and I know it.

blunt.li: Another year here. Still alive.

cheerful.li: Happy anniversary to me! The cook gave me an extra helping.

gloomy.li: Another year survived. I don't know how many more I've got in me.

cold.li: Today makes {YEARS} year(s). I've given this colony more than most.

plain.li: They've taken to calling me {TITLE}. I didn't let on that I'd heard.
Someone said "{TITLE}" today and meant me. I've earned that.

warm.li: They call me {TITLE}. I hope I live up to it.

blunt.li: Known as {TITLE} now. Took them long enough.

cheerful.li: People are calling me {TITLE}! I said it to myself all the way back from the fields.

gloomy.li: So I'm {TITLE}. Something to carve on the headstone, I suppose.

cold.li: A name like {TITLE} opens doors. I'll make use of it.

plain.li: They've started calling me {TITLE}. I'm told it's affectionate. I'm not convinced.
I'm {TITLE} now, apparently. I didn't get a vote.

warm.li: They call me {TITLE}. Well, as long as they're smiling when they say it.

blunt.li: The next person who calls me {TITLE} gets to find out why.

cheerful.li: They call me {TITLE}. Not a compliment, but I'm taking it as one!

gloomy.li: Remembered as {TITLE}. Of all the things.

cold.li: The others have settled on {TITLE} for me. Inaccurate, and it will stick anyway.

plain.li: I told them I'm leaving in three days. They just nodded.
Packing tonight. Not everything. Just what's mine.

warm.li: I don't want to go. Someone, please, give me a reason to stay.

blunt.li: I'm leaving. They had their chances.

cheerful.li: Leaving in three days, for a new start somewhere else! I'm trying to only think about that part.

gloomy.li: I'll probably die out there. It'll still be better than being ignored in here.

cold.li: Departure scheduled. Remaining here is no longer rational.

plain.li: They came again and we're still here, most of us. My hands are still shaking.
Another raid. I can still smell the smoke on my sleeves.
[hurt] Got hurt in the fighting. It hurts to write, so this is all for today.

warm.li: We looked after each other today. That's the part I want to remember.

blunt.li: They came, we fought them off. Same as last time.

cheerful.li: We won! The people I care about are all still breathing.

gloomy.li: One day they'll win. Today we were lucky.

cold.li: Raid repelled. Losses acceptable. The perimeter needs work.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is gone. I keep starting sentences with "we should tell {OTHER_nameDef}".
Lost {OTHER_nameDef} today. Writing the name here so it's written somewhere.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef}, wherever you are, thank you. I didn't say it enough while you were here.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} died. There's nothing to write that would help.

cheerful.li: I can't be cheerful today. {OTHER_nameDef} would tell me to try. Tomorrow.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is dead. I can't see the point of much tonight.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is dead. I find I am not as unaffected as I expected.

plain.li: We held {TRADITION} again this year, so I suppose it's a tradition now.
Someone said "like every year" about {TRADITION} today. I think that makes it ours.
The children were talking about {TRADITION} as if we'd always done it.

warm.li: A tradition of our own: {TRADITION}. I hope the children remember it long after we're gone.

blunt.li: Apparently {TRADITION} is a tradition now. Fine by me, as long as there's food.

cheerful.li: We have a real tradition now, {TRADITION}! I'm already planning next year's.

gloomy.li: So {TRADITION} is ours now. One day someone will keep it up without knowing who started it.

cold.li: Ritual stabilizes morale. Formalizing {TRADITION} is sensible.

plain.li: They made me {OFFICE}. I didn't even put my name forward.
New title: {OFFICE}. Same boots, same mud, more people looking at me.
Two people came to me with complaints before breakfast. I suppose that's the job, now that I'm {OFFICE}.

warm.li: They trust me as {OFFICE}. I won't let them down.

blunt.li: Made {OFFICE}. Anyone with complaints can form a line.

cheerful.li: I'm the {OFFICE}! Practiced my serious face in the washbasin tonight.

gloomy.li: So I'm {OFFICE}. Now it's my fault when things go wrong.

cold.li: Appointed {OFFICE}. A position of leverage. I'll use it well.

plain.li: I'm not {OFFICE} anymore. I'm told it's nothing personal. It feels personal.
Lost the seat. Someone else is {OFFICE} now. I'll be watching how they do.
Got up this morning ready to go about my work as {OFFICE}, and then remembered.

warm.li: No longer {OFFICE}. I hope whoever has it does better than I did.

blunt.li: Kicked out as {OFFICE}. Their mistake.

cheerful.li: Not {OFFICE} anymore, so I get my evenings back!

gloomy.li: They took it away, of course. I was only just getting used to it.

cold.li: Removed as {OFFICE}. Noted who voted against me.

plain.li: They put me back in with the others today. I had that room for {DAYS}.
My room isn't just mine any more. I'm sharing again, and I wasn't asked first.
[winter] Back in shared quarters, in the middle of winter. More breathing in the dark, less sleep.

warm.li: I suppose the room was needed for someone. I still miss it.

blunt.li: They gave me a room and took it back. I won't forget that.

cheerful.li: Out of my room and back with the others. At least the card games are closer now.

gloomy.li: I knew the room wouldn't last. Back to the snoring.

cold.li: My private quarters were reassigned. I'll remember who decided that.
